proposed_paper_claim: State-expanded search models vehicular heading across directed edge pairs (u v) and eliminates 34.1% of sharp turns relative to turn-unaware routing (Condition A1).
supporting_evidence: routing/algorithms.py L460-705; exp_a_corridor_metrics.csv (sharp turns: 32.52 to 21.44; mean diff -11.08; padj=4.5e-5; Cohen dz=-1.0066; Hodges-Lehmann -9.50 turns)
conditions_or_limitations: Evaluated across 25 corridors (N=25, R=5). Condition A1 (turn-unaware state-expanded A*) and Condition A2 (node-level A*) produce deterministic identical vertex sequences across all 25 corridors.
recommended_ieee_wording: Turn-aware state-expanded A* (Condition A0) models vehicular heading across directed edge states (u, v), eliminating 34.1% of sharp maneuvers (>=60 deg) relative to turn-unaware state-expanded routing (Condition A1: 21.44 vs 32.52 turns, padj=4.5e-5, Cohen dz=-1.0066) across 25 metropolitan corridors, while A1 and A2 produce identical route geometries across all 25 corridors.

proposed_paper_claim: The scaled Haversine heuristic h(s) = 0.80 * D_haversine(v t) is admissible.
supporting_evidence: Theorem 1 proof in phase_3_3_corrected_mathematical_claims.md; Lemma 2 spherical geodesic bound; exhaustive scan of bengaluru_graph.pkl (|E|=744216, min multiplier=0.8000, 0 edges < 0.80)
conditions_or_limitations: Conditioned on Assumption A1 (mu(e) >= 0.80 for all edges) and non-negative turn penalties. Implementation allows theoretical 0.76 compounding if an arterial bridge is a roundabout, but exactly 0 instances exist in the active metropolitan network.
recommended_ieee_wording: Under the condition that composite road multipliers satisfy mu(e) >= 0.80 (verified across all 744,216 directed edges in the Bengaluru network), the Haversine distance heuristic scaled by 0.80 is admissible (h(s) <= c*(s)).

proposed_paper_claim: The scaled Haversine heuristic satisfies monotonic consistency and guarantees optimal path finality without state reopening.
supporting_evidence: Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 proofs in phase_3_3_corrected_mathematical_claims.md; spherical triangle inequality on S^2; non-negative turn penalties (P_turn >= 0)
conditions_or_limitations: Applies strictly to state tuples (u, v). Physical road intersections v are expanded up to in-deg(v) times across distinct predecessor arrivals. Initial departure incurs zero turn penalty (Lemma 1).
recommended_ieee_wording: The scaled Haversine heuristic satisfies monotonic consistency (h(s) <= c(s, s') + h(s')), ensuring that each directed edge state (u, v) is finalized upon initial heap extraction without state reopening.

supporting_evidence: exp_b_corridor_metrics.csv (arterial share: 65.05% to 13.84%, padj=8.4e-5, dz=-1.7715; residential share: 13.51% to 44.24%, padj=0.00015, dz=+1.5234)
conditions_or_limitations: Incurs a +15.53% (+1.028 km) physical route distance overhead relative to distance-optimal neutral routing (Condition B1) across the 25 metropolitan corridors.
recommended_ieee_wording: Two-wheeler road impedance weighting significantly suppresses arterial exposure by 51.21 percentage points (13.84% vs 65.05%, padj=8.4e-5, dz=-1.7715) and increases residential street routing (+30.73 pp, padj=0.00015) relative to neutral routing (Condition B1), at a +15.53% detour cost.

proposed_paper_claim: Turn-penalty scaling demonstrates monotonic maneuver reduction; baseline C2 (25/8) represents the empirical corpus-average trade-off knee.
conditions_or_limitations: Empirical Pareto frontier is {C2, C3}. Baseline C2 captures 87.1% of maximum turn reduction while minimizing mean route distance (7.648 km). Universal dominance does not hold across all individual corridors (C2 dominates C3 on 8 corridors, C3 dominates C2 on 7 corridors).
recommended_ieee_wording: Turn sensitivity exhibits monotonic maneuver reduction across penalty tiers (0/0 to 50/16); baseline C2 (25/8) forms the empirical corpus-average trade-off knee, capturing 87.1% of turn reduction while minimizing mean route distance (7.648 km).

proposed_paper_claim: Arterial flyover discounting increases elevated bridge traversal by 148.9%; roundabout modifier operates without spurious route shifts.
supporting_evidence: exp_d_corridor_metrics.csv (bridge traversal: 159.68 m to 397.44 m, +148.9%, distance diff -111.6 m; 0 route changes across non-roundabout corridors)
conditions_or_limitations: Bridge channelization is localized to corridors containing elevated expressways (specifically OD_04 and OD_15). Roundabout modifier produced 0 route geometry changes across evaluated corridors and cannot be claimed as an empirical routing improvement.
recommended_ieee_wording: Arterial flyover discounting (0.80 multiplier) increases elevated bridge traversal by 148.9% (159.68 m to 397.44 m, -111.6 m distance), prominently channelizing Hebbal and Whitefield flyovers, while the roundabout modifier induces no spurious deviations.

proposed_paper_claim: State-expanded A* operates over |E| + 1 states with O(|E|) auxiliary memory and O(|E| log |E|) time complexity on spatial road networks.
supporting_evidence: phase_3_5_final_validation.md Section 1; topological analysis of bengaluru_graph.pkl (max in-deg=6, max out-deg=6, |E_S|=2103894, |E_S|/|E|=2.83)
conditions_or_limitations: Conditioned on Assumption A2 (bounded physical junction valence d_max = O(1)). In general graphs without decrease-key, memory is O(|E| * d_max_in) and time is O(|E| * d_max_in * (log |E| + log d_max_in) + |E| * d_max_in * d_max_out). Stale entries are lazily suppressed from relaxing successors.
recommended_ieee_wording: On spatial road networks where physical intersection valence is bounded (d_max <= 6 in Bengaluru, |E_S|/|E| = 2.83), state-expanded A* operates across |E| + 1 states with O(|E|) auxiliary memory and O(|E| log |E|) time complexity, despite min-heap duplication from the absence of addressable decrease-key.

proposed_paper_claim: Production turn-aware state-expanded A* achieves a median execution runtime of 174.93 ms across 25 metropolitan corridors.
supporting_evidence: exp_a_corridor_metrics.csv (A0 median: 174.93 ms, IQR: 439.08 ms, mean: 382.98 ms +- 464.48 ms, range: 1.01 to 1829.18 ms, N=25, R=5)
conditions_or_limitations: Evaluated on single-threaded Python 3.13 / NetworkX 3.4.2 in-memory graph. 187.62 ms is ablated condition D1 (Bridge Off, Roundabout Off) and must not be cited as baseline. Skewness is an observed empirical distribution across distance tiers, separated from the paired Wilcoxon testing protocol.
recommended_ieee_wording: Production turn-aware routing achieves a median execution runtime of 174.93 ms (IQR 439.08 ms, mean 382.98 ms) across 25 corridors on a 744,216-edge in-memory NetworkX graph, exhibiting an empirically right-skewed runtime distribution across corridor distance tiers.

evidence_type: while turn-penalty heading evaluation incurs a 1.13x median overhead.
conditions_or_limitations: exp_a_corridor_metrics.csv (A2 median: 40.88 ms; A1 median: 154.69 ms; A0 median: 174.93 ms; A1 vs A2 ratio: 3.78x; A0 vs A1 ratio: 1.13x; total A0 vs A2 ratio: 4.28x)

column8: State-space expansion incurs a 3.78x median computational overhead relative to node-level search (Condition A1 vs A2: 154.69 ms vs 40.88 ms), while trigonometric heading evaluation adds a modest 1.13x overhead (Condition A0 vs A1: 174.93 ms vs 154.69 ms), yielding a total 4.28x production overhead.
